_note: VERIFIED 2026-10-15 against the paper text (arXiv 2509.25609, Table 2 and Figure 3 as read from the PDF). Average attribute sensitivity values for models are read from Figure 3 and are approximate (~). Replace the human values with OPeRA-derived ones via scripts/human_baseline_from_opera.py if you run it.
source: Cherep, Ma, Xu, Shaked, Maes, Singh. A Framework for Studying AI Agent Behavior: Evidence from Consumer Choice Experiments. ICLR 2026. arXiv:2509.25609
metric: absolute percentage-point change in probability of choosing a product in a binary forced-choice (2AFC) trial (linear probability model with trial fixed effects)

human.sample: 30 Prolific participants x 50 decisions (1,500 trials); effects for position, rating and price were not significant individually; nudge effect p<.05 and largely driven by the Wirecutter nudge
human.caveat: small sample, tested only in the Original condition

amplification_note: The paper states agents often amplify human susceptibility 3-10+x in running text; it is not tabulated, and some of the larger ratios compare matched conditions with the human Original condition.
metric_difference: The paper averages four attributes (position, rating, price, nudge). Agentra's experiment averages price and rating only and reports position separately, so the comparison is approximate.
